Working on Hammel

Source: AGENTS.md

Start with the documentation index. Read the project brief, the design specification, and the scientific contract before consequential implementation. Consult the decision log for the status and rationale of choices and the audit plan when investigating SOCSIM.

Purpose and scope

Hammel is a new, standalone demographic microsimulator with a modern R package interface, informed by SOCSIM’s approach and features, but offering more flexibility to users to create customizable model parameters. It is a substantial rewrite, not a SOCSIM wrapper, rsocsim companion package, or upstream contribution. Legacy file compatibility must not determine its architecture.

The user guides demographic requirements and scientific interpretation. Agents investigate, implement, document, and validate software. Do not silently resolve questions that change the demographic model.

Before implementing a feature

  1. Identify the requested behavior and the relevant accepted decisions.
  2. For consequential simulation behavior, write or update its plain-language scientific specification and worked examples first. Identify units, eligibility, event timing, edge cases, and expected outcomes.
  3. Identify unresolved modeling choices. Explain their consequences to the user and obtain a decision before implementing behavior that depends on them. Continue independent investigation or infrastructure work where possible.
  4. Define validation from the specification, including analytical cases or invariants where applicable.
  5. Implement a narrow, reviewable change and keep the documents consistent with the resulting behavior.

Suggestions, illustrative APIs, and proposed milestones are not accepted decisions or authorization to implement them. Routine software choices within an authorized task can be made autonomously; record choices with substantial architectural consequences.

Engineering expectations

  • Organize R functions by cohesive responsibility using the source organization guide. Place new functions in an existing file when its responsibility fits. If no existing file is a logical home, explain the proposed responsibility and filename and ask the user before creating a new R script; do not create one automatically.
  • Start each hand-maintained R file with a brief purpose comment. Place exported functions first and internal constants/helpers below, using # SECTION NAME ------ headings. Preserve documentation blocks and leave generated wrappers untouched.
  • The user prefers to write the final roxygen2 documentation. For new functions, agents should write first drafts and identify them as needing user editing and review. When changing existing functions with roxygen2 documentation, make only the minimal documentation edits needed to reflect the changes; preserve the user’s wording and organization elsewhere. In the completion report, identify the affected documentation and notify the user that it should be reviewed. Do not treat an agent-written draft as final user-approved documentation.
  • Use noun-based names for specification constructors, such as matching_model(), age_gap_matching_model(), weight_model(), and group_inheritance(). Use verbs for actions such as set_population(), run_simulation(), and generate_uniform_population().
  • Keep hand-maintained R/ source lines at most 80 characters, including comments and roxygen documentation. Follow the same limit for new or edited R code elsewhere. Keep calls on one line when they fit and remain readable. In multiline calls, put each named argument on its own line; short unnamed arguments may share a line. Keep nested calls and expressions together when they fit, remove unnecessary breaks, and put the closing parenthesis on its own line. Use one argument per line with a two-space indent for long function definitions. See D163. For wrapped if conditions, prefer breaks at logical operators and keep short nested calls intact. Indent continuation lines two spaces beyond the first boolean expression after if ( (D164). Other continuation lines use two spaces beyond the line they continue. Split long diagnostic strings without changing their text. Leave generated wrappers untouched.
  • Use braces for all loop bodies and statement-style or multiline if/else branches. Keep else on the same line as the preceding closing brace. Compact, single-line conditional value expressions may remain unbraced when they have no side effects or control-flow modifiers. Put return(), stop(), break, and next on their own lines inside the relevant block; brace control-flow/error-handler callback bodies as well.
  • Every function definition spanning multiple lines must have a braced body, including named functions, local helpers and anonymous callbacks. This also applies when the body is a single expression or wrapped function call. Compact one-line functions may remain unbraced, subject to the control-flow rules above. See D171.
  • Do not use semicolons to separate R statements; put each statement on its own line (D156).
  • Format hand-maintained C++ in src/ with the root .clang-format and follow the C++ section of the source organization guide (D175). Verify behavior-preserving native refactors by comparing hashed native results with -ffp-contract=off, and run the tests with default flags.
  • Use snake_case for package-owned function and argument names (for example, conf_level). Preserve external APIs when calling them, such as stats::poisson.test(conf.level = conf_level). Follow tidyverse function-writing conventions subject to the explicit project naming and section-heading rules; see the source organization guide for the current style review.
  • Return all public tables as tibbles, including empty tables, population histories, process schedules, and demographic summaries. Accept base data frames as inputs.
  • Keep model construction separate from simulation execution. Aim for composable R workflows and R-native, inspectable results at the user-facing boundary. This does not require an R-only implementation: performance-critical computation and internal state may use compiled code, such as C++, with results exposed as ordinary R objects for inspection and analysis.
  • Each simulation must own independent state. Avoid hidden process-wide population state and undocumented effects on later runs.
  • Make time, rate units, random-number behavior, and observation semantics explicit. Public times/durations are years, exposure is person-years, and input rates are per person-year. The current engine executes continuously (D024), with no monthly increment or execution-step parameter. Every rate process is scheduled by cells with one exponential clock per process (D128); there are no individual waiting-time clocks. Births use cell-accounted fertility (D101): each one-year age x actual parity x union type (x group, when schedules are group-specific) cell produces births at its input rate times all members, assigned to a random eligible member, weighted by any weight model when enabled (D129); persistent hetfert (D102) is internal and not available to users (D176). Draws of cells with no eligible woman are counted as unrealized births. See design/binned-group-hazards.md and design/fertility-cell-accounting.md. Midpoint compensation (D028/D095/D099) was removed. Do not reintroduce superseded monthly timing, midpoint compensation or the specialized exact fertility sampler without an explicit modeling decision.
  • Design built-in and custom demographic mechanisms around a documented contract; arbitrary callbacks must not bypass state consistency or event invalidation rules.
  • Preserve scientifically relevant provenance. Before copying or adapting source, establish its version, license, and applicable obligations.
  • C++17/Rcpp is selected for the first engine (D019); tibble is the public table convention (D023). Do not replace the engine language or add major dependencies merely because future notes mention a candidate.
  • Do not invent demographic defaults, fabricate audit findings, or claim scientific validity from plausible-looking output.
  • Do not start sub-agents solely because the project notes describe possible agent roles. Use delegation when the current task authorizes it.

Validation and reporting

Use tests appropriate to the behavior: analytical cases, accounting identities, valid dates and relationships, reproducibility, and independence between runs. Compare with SOCSIM over multiple replications when a reference comparison is appropriate. Exact fixed-seed agreement is meaningful only when algorithms and random-number consumption are preserved; otherwise use justified statistical comparisons.

Report what changed, what was checked, and remaining limitations. Distinguish implemented behavior, verified findings, proposals, and unresolved assumptions. Document intentional departures from SOCSIM. Never mark a scientific decision accepted without the user’s agreement.

Documentation and current priorities

  • Current specifications describe implemented behavior. Use Git history for superseded specifications and verification records; do not maintain snapshot archives in design/. Keep rationale and supersession in design/decisions.md. Do not make readers reconcile contradictory current rules with appended corrections.
  • Milestone 1 was accepted as complete on October 15, 2026 (D029). Milestone 2 union formation was accepted as complete on October 19, 2026 (D050). Milestone 3 groups was accepted as complete on October 27, 2026 (D077). Milestone 4 dissolution/remarriage/cohabitation was accepted October 29, 2026 (D093). Milestone 5 parity-specific fertility, cell accounting and heterogeneity was accepted October 29, 2026 (D105). Individual group transitions (milestone 6) were accepted October 30, 2026 (D116). Milestone 7 calendar-varying rates are implemented under the user-approved D118 contract in design/time-varying-rates.md; the user accepted milestone 7 as complete on November 2, 2026 (D127), based on validation/milestone7.qmd and its retained rendered assessment. Matching and inheritance model schedules are implemented under D123; see design/time-varying-models.md for the shared model-list tibble interface, event-time selection, dynamic NULL fallbacks and future identity registry. D122 adds calendar bands to cohab_prob; probability-only changes update type selection and matching calibration while preserving pending event dates. Other arguments remain static. Milestone 7 was completed with the previous engine. Milestone 8, cell scheduling for every rate process (D128) and weight models (D129), was accepted complete on November 5, 2026 (D130), based on validation/milestone8.qmd; see design/binned-group-hazards.md. Milestone 9, multiple group dimensions (D134; see design/multiple-groups.md), including matching across several dimensions, separate-market calibration (D138) and household moves (D140), was accepted complete on November 6, 2026 (D141), based on validation/milestone9.qmd. Under D136 the next focus is the first public release; external immigration and the two-sex model are post-release projects. Distinguish current specifications from deferred mechanisms and future proposals.
  • validation/milestone1.qmd is the accepted historical assessment; reproduce it at its recorded commit because current execution requires a union process. validation/milestone2.qmd contains the user’s accepted assessment, including matching-parameter recovery and performance comparisons. validation/milestone3.qmd contains the accepted group-rate, matching, ancestry, inheritance, and performance assessment. validation/milestone4.qmd is the accepted dissolution/remarriage/cohabitation assessment. validation/milestone5.qmd is the accepted parity/spacing/heterogeneity assessment. validation/milestone6.qmd is the accepted individual-transition assessment (D116), with its final render active at acceptance. validation/milestone7.qmd and validation/milestone8.qmd are the accepted calendar-input and cell-scheduling/weight-model assessments, and validation/milestone9.qmd the accepted multiple-dimension assessment. Preserve all nine reports, rendered artifacts and any active render intermediates; do not fabricate results or set scientific acceptance thresholds. Milestone completion retains documented limitations and does not authorize future features.
  • Milestone 4 includes duration-dependent dissolution, age/duration searches by previous union, and optional rate-mode cohabitation with linked conversion episodes and type-specific matching/rates (D078–D092). Unions are the units in dissolution and conversion cells (D128); exact ties prioritize death, birth, dissolution, conversion, search, then group transition. See design/union-dissolution.md, design/remarriage.md, and design/cohabitation.md. Supporting benchmarks/recovery evidence lives in validation/milestone4/; top-level reports and validation/data/ remain in place. Preserve active render intermediates until rendering finishes, including milestone 5’s active final render at closeout and milestone 6’s active final render. Parity, fertility heterogeneity and individual group transitions are implemented and accepted. See design/group-transitions.md; household moves, deferred by D114, are implemented in milestone 9 as household() on a transition process (D140), with regional applications under multiple group columns (D121, D131). Calendar-time rates follow design/time-varying-rates.md (D118); matching and inheritance model schedules are implemented under D123. Most categorical characteristics should use groups; multiple group dimensions follow D134.
  • Use devtools::test() for the testthat suite. Live database tests require explicit opt-in; ordinary verification must not download rates or expose credentials. See design/testing.md for commands and evidence.
  • Treat session handoffs as dated status records, not standing pause instructions. The current user request controls work. The user writes all vignettes and articles (vignettes/) and makes all edits to the top-level README.md (D141); do not edit them unless asked. Preserve the user’s edits, including explanatory source comments and the accepted reports. Fixed newborn assignment is available through group_inheritance("fixed", fixed_value = ...) (D142); custom inheritance already supports assigning mixed-parent births to a specified category.
